verdicts.why: 'talk' is the lemma of 話す, a component of 話し合う => 'discuss'; the row is about its own sentence, but 'talk' is not in the seed target 'they think that we need to discuss the problem'.
何も glosses 'anything', which the seed 'I didn't do much on Sunday' does not render as a separate word; this is a literal gloss of a word the translation dropped.
'isn't' glosses ありません, but the seed 'my name is not very unusual' has 'is not' rather than the contraction.
'could you (polite)?' glosses いただけますか, but the seed 'can you tell me what your name is?' has 'can you'; the LEGO also says 'can you', so this is a literal gloss of the polite form.
The target is a grammatical label '(progressive: -ing / are ~ing)', not text from the seed 'I think that you're doing very well'; it is a gloss of the ている form, which is in the sentence.
'not much' glosses あまり, but the seed 'I didn't do much on Sunday' has 'didn't do much'; the words are present but interposed by the contraction 'didn't'.

すべて => 'everything' has no counterpart in 'He didn't want to look after the young dog all afternoon' and looks like a mis-gloss of ずっと ('all'); but the LEGO 午後ずっと => 'all afternoon' is taught by sibling C02 plus the LEGO itself, so a fix to 'all' is possible but not forced, and cutting is not proven.
丈夫 => 'strong' is a literal split of 大丈夫, which the seed 'no problem. Everything is okay' renders as 'okay'; the row is about its sentence's word, so this is not a provable orphan.
ありません => 'there isn't' is a literal gloss of part of 問題ありません => 'no problem', which the seed 'no problem. Everything is okay' contains; 'there isn't' is not a substring.
〜ていた => 'was -ing' glosses part of 以前〜していた => 'used to' in the seed 'my friend used to work in an office'; the progressive tense label is not in the seed target.
言っている => 'you are saying' is a literal gloss, while the seed 'I don't know who you mean' renders it as 'you mean'; the words are reworded by the translation.
'a man' is not contiguous in the seed 'an old man' because 'old' is interposed; the row is about its own sentence (男の人 => man), so it is not an orphan.
前に => 'earlier' glosses a word the seed 'can you tell me something else before I answer?' renders as 'before'; this is a literal gloss, and the row is about its sentence.
前に => 'earlier' glosses a word the seed 'you're like someone I used to know' renders as 'used to'; this is a literal gloss, and the row is about its sentence.
'I've got' glosses ことがあります, while the seed 'Have you got more to learn?' has 'Have you got' as an inverted question; the words 'got' are present but the person and order differ.
でした => 'past' is a grammatical label, not text in the seed 'we didn't want to let anyone hear the truth'; it glosses a tense marker the translation renders through 'didn't'.
か => 'question' is a label for the question particle, which the seed 'Have you got more to learn?' renders only through word order and the question mark.
似た => 'resembling' is a literal gloss of the word that the seed 'you shouldn't worry about doing something similar' renders as 'similar'; it is the lemma-like form, not a substring.
です => 'am' is a copula gloss; the seed 'I like feeling as if I'm nearly ready to go' contains 'I'm', not a standalone 'am', and 好きです => 'I like' makes it a back-gloss.
できます => 'be able to' glosses a word that the seed 'when will you be ready to start?' renders as 'be ready'; the LEGO says 'be ready', so the row is a literal gloss of the verb.
